name: Mentimeter
tagline: Interactive presentations with live polls, quizzes and word clouds the audience answers from their phones.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanic is not hard: a room code, a websocket, a bar chart that grows as answers land. An agent can give you a working presenter view, a phone-friendly voting page, multiple choice, open text, a scale question and a crude word cloud in a weekend. What breaks is everything around it: 200 people on hotel wifi hitting your laptop, the slide editor that makes it look like a real deck, the PowerPoint and Teams add-ins, and the quiet assumption that menti.com will be up when you are standing in front of a room. Build it for your own team standup or classroom and it is genuinely fine. Build it for a client workshop and you will spend the first five minutes apologising for the join link.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local web app where you create poll questions, project a room code, and watch a live chart update as participants answer from their phones.
requirements: a machine that can be reached by participants: either same wifi with a LAN IP, or a cheap VPS / tunnel for a public URL
participants with phones and a browser
whatYouLose: Reliability at crowd scale: your laptop plus hotel wifi is not a CDN, and the failure happens live in front of people
The actual presentation editor: slide layouts, themes, fonts, images, so you end up pairing your polls with a separate deck
PowerPoint, Google Slides, Teams and Zoom integrations, which is how most people actually run these
Polished question types: proper word cloud layout, quiz leaderboards with timing and points, ranking, 2x2 grids
Result exports, per-session history, and sharing a results link with people who were not in the room
moatNotes: The hard part is not the poll, it is being the thing 300 strangers can load at the same time without you thinking about it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product is used in the one moment where you cannot debug. People pay for a join URL audiences recognise, servers that absorb a conference room spike, and quiz and word cloud rendering that looks deliberate on a projector. A self-hosted clone is great for recurring internal use where you control the room and the stakes are low, and a bad idea the first time you present to people who are paying you.
notes: Fine for your own standups and lectures, risky for anything you would call a workshop.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted live audience polling app, like a minimal Mentimeter, in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with Express and Socket.IO
- better-sqlite3 for storage, file at ./data/polls.db
- Server-rendered HTML with EJS, plain CSS, no build step, no framework
- qrcode npm package to render the join QR as a data URL

What to build:
1. Presenter side at /admin, protected by a single ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env via a cookie session. Create a "session" containing an ordered list of questions.
2. Question types: multiple choice (2-8 options), open text, and scale 1-5. Nothing else.
3. Presenter view at /present/:sessionId shows the current question full screen, large, dark background, with a big room code and a QR code pointing at the join URL. Results update live: horizontal bars for choice and scale, a scrolling list of submissions for open text. Arrow keys move between questions and push the change to all connected participants over Socket.IO.
4. Participant view at /join and /r/:code is phone-first: enter code, see only the question the presenter is currently on, tap or type an answer, see a "thanks" state, wait for the next question. One vote per question per browser, enforced with a random participant id in localStorage plus a unique index in SQLite. No accounts.
5. Room codes: 6 digits, unique among active sessions.
6. /present/:sessionId/results.csv exports all answers for that session.

Rules:
- Everything is local: no telemetry, no analytics, no third-party JS, no CDN links. Bundle nothing you do not need.
- Secrets in .env: ADMIN_PASSWORD, PORT, PUBLIC_BASE_URL (used to build the join URL and QR, so it works over LAN IP or a tunnel).
- Handle reconnects: on socket connect, participants re-sync to the presenter's current question index.
- Out of scope, do not build: slide editor, images, themes, quizzes with scoring or timers, word clouds, user accounts, multi-presenter, PowerPoint integration.
- Include a README with setup, a note on how to expose it over LAN vs a tunnel, and an honest warning that this is sized for roughly a few dozen participants, not a conference hall.
